messages:
leo: heads-up from the monthly access sweep: infra-ci-runner@svcacct has cloudkms.* permissions across 4 projects. looks like old CI pipelines share a single keyring. potential lateral-movement vector. :thinking:

tara: ouch. can you share the quick audit query you used so we can reproduce?

leo: sure. query against CloudAuditLogs export in BigQuery:

```sql
SELECT protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail AS principal,
       resourceName,
       COUNT(*) as hits
FROM `redwood-audit.cloudaudit_googleapis_com_*` 
WHERE protoPayload.serviceName = 'cloudkms.googleapis.com'
  AND TIMESTAMP(protoPayload.timestamp) > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 180 DAY)
GROUP BY principal, resourceName
HAVING COUNT(*) > 2
ORDER BY hits DESC;
```

henry: good. that's the pattern i've seen before when CI runners were spun up during onboarding and never scoped. i'd recommend: (1) create per-pipeline keyrings, (2) rotate master key, (3) revoke old role from infra-ci-runner and rebind to scoped keys.

neha: for risk mgmt, propose a two-step safe plan: A) roll new keys and update a single low-risk pipeline to use them (canary), B) run pipeline for 48h, watch decrypt errors and job failures, C) if green, rotate remaining pipelines in batches of 5.

leo: agreed. add audit evidence steps: snapshot current key IAM policy and save to gs://redwood-audit/kms-snapshots/${thread_ts}/pre-policy.json and attach ticket ID. Also log the commit SHA that updates pipeline config.

devops-bot: ticket created: INFRA-4921 (CI KMS entitlement cleanup). owner=henry. due=2026-04-02.

tara: small nit: how will we handle secrets stored encrypted with the old key? some jobs decrypt artifacts at runtime. we need a migration path or cross-keys ACL.

henry: plan: create new key with same cryptoProfile, add new key to keyring, update pipeline to use new key, keep old key for 7 days and monitor decrypts, then schedule secure destroy. cross-key rewrap not needed if we update producers/consumers. documenting steps in runbook.

neha: monitoring signals: KMS AccessDenied rate by principal, job failure rate for pipelines that use KMS, number of re-encrypt operations. set alert: >5 AccessDenied in 30m for the canary pipeline = immediate rollback.

leo: exact gcloud commands we plan to run (example):

# snapshot
```bash
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy projects/PROJ/locations/global/keyRings/shared/cryptoKeys/master-key \
  --project=PROJ > pre-policy-${thread_ts}.json
gsutil cp pre-policy-${thread_ts}.json gs://redwood-audit/kms-snapshots/${thread_ts}/pre-policy.json
```

# revoke old binding
```bash
gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding projects/PROJ/locations/global/keyRings/shared/cryptoKeys/master-key \
  --member='serviceAccount:infra-ci-runner@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com' \
  --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter'
```

# grant scoped binding
```bash
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/PROJ/locations/global/keyRings/pipelineX/cryptoKeys/kx \
  --member='serviceAccount:infra-ci-runner@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com' \
  --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter'
```

tara: can we avoid a full revoke during the canary? maybe add a conditional binding with a tag or timestamp to limit access during the test window.

henry: good idea. optional conditional snippet:```yaml
- role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
  members:
  - 'serviceAccount:infra-ci-runner@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com'
  condition:
    title: canary-window
    expression: request.time < timestamp("2026-04-05T00:00:00Z")
```

neha: ops checklist request from compliance: include justification blob for each entitlement change. suggested bullets: prior role + snapshot path, reason (unused/shared-key risk), mitigation (scoped key + rotation), verification items (no AccessDenied, job run success), ticket link.

leo: i've added that template to INFRA-4921. also created a regression alert to watch for re-grants: if the same principal gets roles/cloudkms.* re-added within 30d, auto-create an incident for review.

sec-bot: scheduled run: canary for INFRA-4921 on 2026-03-28T15:00:00Z, owner=henry.

henry: i'll run the canary against pipeline-alpha (non-prod). plan window 48h. will post logs to gs://redwood-audit/kms-snapshots/${thread_ts}/canary-logs.txt and paste greps here.

tara: ok. once canary is green, we want a phased automation: script that iterates pipelines.json and issues key rebinds with a 24h delay between batches. also include a dry-run mode.

neha: add me as reviewer for compliance artifacts. i'll sign-off before final revoke.

leo: summary action items: HENRY run canary + post logs; TARA add automation dry-run and batch plan; NEHA review compliance artifacts; LEO snapshot policies and update ticket. target decision = 2026-04-01 EOD. :lock: :gear:

henry: on schedule, ping if you need the canary window adjusted.
